title: Account Manager, Corporate

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our Customer Success team is made up of Product Specialists and Account Managers who are passionate about helping our clients succeed. We partner with a diverse range of organizations, from Fortune 1000 companies to some of the largest financial institutions globally.

While key performance indicators include retention rate and the identification of growth opportunities, the responsibilities of Account Managers go much deeper. The team also extracts a wealth of knowledge from our clients, bringing that internally to product, marketing and sales teams in order to maximize the effectiveness of our business’ strategy and communication.

title: Technical Team Lead (Full-stack)
description:
Who We Are

Yellow Card is the largest licensed Stablecoin-based infrastructure provider operating across over 60 countries. From Stablecoin payment infrastructure to fiat settlement rails,  wallet services, and custom local Stablecoin issuance, Yellow Card provides the complete infrastructure businesses need to manage Stablecoins, payments, and operations across 50 emerging markets.

Yellow Card operates with a substantial global team spanning 24 countries. This workforce is characterized by its linguistic diversity, with collective speaking of over 25 languages, underscoring the company’s extensive international reach.

We’re looking to hire a Technical Team Lead located within Africa to join our fast-growing, fully remote team. You will join our Commercial Pod , the team that owns the systems our commercial business runs on: trade execution, treasury operations, commercial operations, and the internal tooling our operations teams use every day. These systems handle real money in real time, across multiple currencies and regulators.

 

As a Technical Team Lead , you will own architecture, lead the hardest implementations yourself, and set the standard for how the pod builds. This is deliberately not a management role. Your Engineering Manager handles 1:1s, performance, and growth conversations. You own technical direction and technical quality, and you stay deep in the code, with roughly 90% of your time hands-on.

 

This role is full-stack by requirement, not by preference. Our commercial surfaces span a Vue 3 B2B portal and a fleet of TypeScript services on AWS, and the interesting problems, such as how a rate is fetched, cached, priced, displayed, and then traded against, cut straight across that boundary. We need someone who can hold the whole path in their head and make calls at either end.

 

Candidates with experience in FinTech or Crypto products are strongly preferred. We value clear communication, strong ownership, and engineers who raise the bar for everyone around them.

 

Our technology stack includes: TypeScript, Node.js, Vue 3 (Composition API), Pinia, Vite, Vitest, Storybook, Serverless Framework, AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, RDS, AWS SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions, EKS with Helm and Istio, Valkey and ElastiCache, S3, API Gateway, Cognito, AWS Bedrock, Datadog, GitHub Actions, and more.

What You'll Do

• Own the architecture of Commercial Pod systems end-to-end: service boundaries, data models, event flows, and the contracts between our frontend and our services

• Lead the pod’s design doc process. Write the hard ones, review the rest, and run the design doc review sessions where designs get pressure-tested before anyone writes code

• Represent Commercial in our org-wide engineering standards programme, reviewing RFCs as a Technical Lead and driving their adoption inside the pod: auditing existing services against approved standards and sequencing the gap-closing work

• Make and document the trade-offs. Serverless versus containerised, synchronous versus event-driven, build versus integrate. Then explain the reasoning so the pod can make the next call without you

• Take the highest-risk production implementations yourself, building across both the Vue 3 frontend and our TypeScript serverless and containerised services

• Set the engineering bar through your own code and your reviews: strict typing, real test coverage, structured logs, correlation IDs, graceful failure handling, and fault tolerance as a design goal rather than an aspiration

• Own the production health of Commercial services: meaningful Datadog dashboards, monitors and SLOs with thresholds that reflect reality, and alerts a person can act on at 3 am

• Lead incident response and root cause analysis for Commercial systems, and make sure the follow-up work actually ships

• Take part in the technical lead dev support rota, roughly once every five weeks.

• Mentor the engineers in the pod, growing their architectural judgement and not ju

title: SaaS Sales Development Representative - Illinois (Remote)
description:
About Cargobase

Founded in 2013, Cargobase was created to transform how shippers and logistics service providers collaborate. What started as a solution to simplify spot-freight procurement quickly evolved into the leading enterprise platform in this space.

Today, Cargobase helps global enterprise shippers such as Bosch, Goodyear, Reckitt Benckiser, and Textron work seamlessly with logistics service providers including DHL, DSV, and FedEx. Our transportation management platform brings all parties together in a single interface, streamlining spot-buy freight from quoting and booking to tracking, invoicing, and analytics. Delivering transparency, efficiency, and control at scale.

Role Overview

As a SaaS Sales Development Representative, you are responsible for driving top-of-funnel performance by identifying, engaging, and qualifying new prospects to build a predictable and high-quality sales pipeline. You play a critical role at the start of the sales cycle, assessing customer fit, clearly articulating Cargobase’s value proposition, and ensuring only well-qualified opportunities are passed to Account Executives.

This role requires disciplined outreach, strong qualification judgment, and consistent CRM hygiene. As the first point of contact for many prospects, you represent Cargobase in the market, strengthening our brand while directly contributing to sustainable pipeline growth and revenue impact.

Key Responsibilities

1. Lead Generation & Pipeline Creation

• Identify, source, and qualify new prospects across target industries and geographies.

• Apply structured outreach via email, phone, and social channels to maintain a predictable inflow of high-quality leads.

• Validate customer fit quickly using defined qualification criteria (i.e.use case, urgency, business pain).

• Progress only leads to the sales pipeline to ensure quality and accuracy.

2. Pipeline Ownership 

• Manage the initial qualification stages of the pipeline, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and consistency in opportunity creation.

• Maintain complete and up-to-date CRM records across all lead activities.

3. Introductory Solution Selling

• Identify prospect pain points and articulate Cargobase’s high-level value proposition.

• Align prospect needs with core platform capabilities during early conversations.

• Set accurate expectations to avoid misalignment during later sales stages.

4. Forecasting, Reporting & Target Achievement

• Provide accurate forecasts on lead volumes, qualification rates, and conversion metrics.

• Track outreach activities through CRM and ensure strong data hygiene for visibility to Sales Leadership.

• Consistently meet or exceed monthly and quarterly targets for qualified opportunities.

Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Supply Chain, or a related field (fresh graduates welcome).

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Organised, self-motivated, and comfortable managing a high volume of outreach.

• Genuine curiosity about logistics, technology, or enterprise sales.

• Familiarity with CRM tools or outreach platforms is a plus, but not required.

• Comfortable in a fast-paced, multicultural, and data-driven environment.

Benefits

• Competitive base salary plus  uncapped performance bonuses.

• 21 days annual leave  plus all national public holidays.

• Additional  Years of Service Leave .

• 401(k) plan  with  employer matching.

• Comprehensive  medical, dental, and vision insurance .

• Flexible wellness benefit  for gym memberships and more. 

• Opportunity to work in a fast-growing global technology company with strong career growth potential.

• Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field. *(High school diploma+ 7 yrs Linux system administration experience may be substituted for degree)

• Proven experience as a System Administrator operating within an AWS environment.

• Hands-on experience supporting Department of War (DoW) or U.S. Air Force IT environments.

• Experience administering Linux operating systems (AWS Linux, Ubuntu) as well as Microsoft Windows Server environments.

• Must have extensive experience hardening servers and applications in accordance with DISA STIGs.

• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manipulate operating system components and optimize performance.

• Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

title: Founding G2M & Sales Manager - DACH & Nordics (gn) @ AI Digital Defense Venture,
description:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.
About the Venture
We build frontier artificial intelligence that helps governments and defence organisations make sense of a fast-moving information environment. Our systems help the teams responsible for national security read a complex information environment faster and clearer than ever before. We've closed a pre-seed round and are already running live government pilots, with plans to expand across Europe and beyond. This is an early, venture-backed company doing work that carries weight.
About the Role
This is a founding role for our expansion across the DACH region and the Nordics. You will own how we grow here, from the first conversation through to a signed contract, building the region much as we built the UK: learning the landscape, opening doors, landing pilots and turning them into long-term contracts. You will work closely with the founders and with a forward-deployed engineer who builds the tools, integrations and prototypes that a live sales process needs, so your job is to win the room, work out what the customer actually needs, and direct that build until the deal closes.
What you'll do

• Own go-to-market across the DACH region and the Nordics, winning and growing contracts across government, defence and large enterprise, from first conversation through to close.

• Map the region from a blank slate, find the advisory relationships that open doors, and build a network where we do not have one yet.

• Land pilots and turn them into long-term contracts, working from first engagements towards enterprise deals worth seven figures a year.

• Turn customer needs into scoped solutions, briefing and directing a forward-deployed engineer to stand up the reports, dashboards, integrations and prototypes that move deals forward.

• Build the regional playbook from first principles: pipeline, qualification, pricing and close.

• Make complex technology clear and convincing to senior decision-makers in government and defence.

• Work directly with the founders on strategy, positioning and the deals that matter most.

About You
You are, at heart, someone who likes to build something from nothing. You are at your best finding the first contacts, earning their trust, and turning a cold market into real relationships and real deals. You are hands-on, as comfortable doing the sourcing and outreach yourself as sitting across from a senior decision-maker on a sensitive brief, and you understand that this kind of work is slow, careful and built on trust.

• A real appetite for business development: you like winning deals, opening relationships and building a market from scratch, and you keep going long after an inherited network has run dry.

• Enough of a technical background to scope solutions, brief an engineer and hold your own with technical buyers.

• The drive to build a process from nothing rather than run one that already exists.

• Fluency in the region: strong English and at least one relevant regional language, with German a clear advantage.

• Comfort in an early startup, where there is real ownership, quick decisions and plenty of ambiguity.

• Discretion and integrity, because our work depends on a high level of trust.

• A background in defence, national security or another setting where you have earned trust and done deals with government is a strong advantage.

• Eligibility for security clearance is an advantage.

Why Join
This is a launching role with a whole region to own, at an early, venture-backed company that has already closed a pre-seed round and is running live pilots with government. You will work alongside the founders, with founder-level access and ownership from the start, and the market you build will be yours to shape. The work is demanding and it matters, for clients operating at a high level on problems that are genuinely difficult. For the person who builds this well, there is meaningful equity and real upside.

title: Product Analyst
description:
Established in 2021, Independence Pet Holdings is a corporate holding company that manages a diverse and broad portfolio of modern pet health brands and services, including insurance, pet education, lost recovery services, and more throughout North America.
We believe pet insurance is more than a financial product and build solutions to simplify the pet parenting journey and help improve the well-being of pets. As a leading authority in the pet category, we operate with a full stack of resources, capital, and services to support pet parents. Our multi-brand and omni-channel approach include our own insurance carrier, insurance brands and partner brands.
Job Summary:
As a Product Analyst at Independence Pet Holdings , you will directly influence the performance, competitiveness, and regulatory strength of our pet insurance portfolio. You will analyze product performance, identify rate and underwriting opportunities, and support the development of insurance products that balance customer value with profitable growth.
Working closely with Product Management, Actuarial, and Underwriting, you will apply your insurance analytics expertise to evaluate loss trends, rate adequacy, pricing assumptions, and portfolio health. Your insights will guide decisions that ensure our products remain compliant, competitive, and aligned with carrier and MGA strategic objectives.
This role is ideal for someone who understands the nuances of insurance product performance and is motivated by the opportunity to shape the future of pet insurance.
Key Responsibilities

•
Portfolio Performance Analysis - Analyze product and portfolio P&L, including earned premium, loss ratios, frequency/severity trends, rate adequacy, and underwriting performance to identify profit and growth opportunities.

•
Insurance KPI Reporting - Develop and enhance reporting tools that support carrier and MGA decision‑making, including dashboards for rate actions, retention, claims trends, and regulatory performance.

•
Product & Rating Expertise - Serve as a subject matter expert on pet insurance contracts, rating structures, underwriting guidelines, and state‑specific product variations.

•
Data Integrity & Analysis - Work with structured data from multiple systems (policy admin, claims, rating engines, distribution partners) to generate accurate, actionable insights.

•
Ad Hoc Insurance Analysis - Conduct deep‑dive analyses on emerging issues such as loss spikes, rate need, regulatory changes, or underwriting leakage.

•
Underwriting & Actuarial Collaboration - Partner with Actuarial and Underwriting to evaluate rate indications, monitor product performance, and support filings, forms updates, and pricing changes.

•
Product Monitoring & Compliance Support - Support ongoing product maintenance, including monitoring regulatory requirements, state variations, and DOI‑related impacts on product strategy.

•
Strategic Portfolio Consultation - Provide recommendations on product strategy, pricing actions, underwriting adjustments, and market opportunities based on analytical trends.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent work experience.

•
2+ years of experience in P&C or pet insurance analytics , pricing, product management, or underwriting.

• Strong understanding of insurance KPIs (loss ratio, combined ratio, rate adequacy, retention, frequency/severity).

• Proficiency with analytical tools such as SQL, SAS, R, Python , and visualization platforms like Power BI or Tableau .

• Experience working with insurance data sources (policy admin systems, claims data, rating engines, underwriting rules).

• Ability to communicate complex insurance concepts to both technical and non‑technical audiences.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment.

title: Director, Growth (São Paulo, BR)
Product Manager (Senior/Staff-level)
description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Synthesia ships more product, faster, than we ever have. AI has collapsed the cost of building which means the hard part is no longer making things, it’s making sure people actually adopt them. That’s the job of Growth, and we’re changing how we do it: instead of bolting Growth on after launch to optimise, we’re embedding a Growth PM into every core bet from day one, so how a product acquires, activates and scales is designed in from the first cycle.

We’re hiring a Growth Product Manager to own the Growth surface for one of those bets and help build a growth-led way of working across the company.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

- Own Growth for a core product area end to end, acquisition, activation, adoption and retention, baked into the roadmap from the start, not retrofitted.

- Partner closely with the core product PMs and engineers who own the surface, bringing high-impact growth ideas and working out where they fit, and getting the primitives exposed that let you build and scale on top.

- Design growth into the product itself: discovery-led acquisition loops, and experiences that get users to their job-to-be-done in a couple of clicks (sometimes without opening the editor at all).

- Rally teams around specific, measurable outcomes and help each one hit its goal faster through what you build together.

- Work across engineering, marketing and GTM to make funnel- and journey-thinking a normal part of how we build.

WHO YOU ARE

- AI-native. You’ve driven AI into how a product or team works - not just worked somewhere that does AI. You use it daily, you’re curious about how the stack works, and you keep up as it moves (fast).

- Scrappy and comfortable in ambiguity. You’ve taken something 0→1, you move fast, and you don’t need a clean brief or a stable roadmap to make progress. Constant change energises you rather than blocking you.

- A builder of credibility. You win trust across teams quickly and can get engineers, PMs and GTM aligned around growth - even when that’s a new way of working for them.

- Technically fluent and genuinely curious. You can hold your own with engineers on how things work and where the trade-offs are.

- Outcome-driven. You anchor on the right metric and move it.

REQUIREMENTS

- Experience as a Product Manager with exposure to Growth. Depth in a single specific lever is a plus, not a prerequisite.

- Demonstrable experience driving AI-native product or ways of working.

- Comfortable in a fast-moving, 0→1, frequently-disrupted environment.

- Strong communication and the personality to build credibility and influence across functions.

- Technical fluency to partner credibly with engineering.

LOCATION

Remote from Europe or hybrid based from our London or Munich offices.

 

OUR CULTURE

At Synthesia we’re passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here. https://www.notion.so/How-we-work-at-S

About your new role:
CommandLink 's vendor ecosystem is the backbone of how we deliver connectivity and services to our customers, and this role will own the relationship between CommandLink and our vendors from the data side up. Today our team manages a large volume of vendor information that constantly needs to be tracked, verified, and updated across our systems, starting with our Quote Tool, which holds the most complete picture we have of each vendor and client. Keeping that tool accurate and current is critical to how the whole business operates.
We're looking for a Vendor Operations Analyst who doesn't just plan around the data, but who gets into the platform and does the work: tracking down information, entering it into the system, and analyzing it to surface insights. You'll work hands on with vendor and platform data every day, and you'll be a key point of contact for vendors, Sales, and other internal stakeholders. This isn't a deeply technical role, but it does require someone analytical, comfortable navigating systems and tools, and confident enough to bring a commercial mindset to every conversation.
Key Responsibilities:

• Own and maintain the Quote Tool, rate cards, and building lists/zip codes, making sure they always hold the most complete and accurate vendor and client information possible, and work toward a single source of truth for all vendor data.

• Acquire vendor information (building lists, rate cards, API capabilities, contact and escalation matrices), load it into the Platform, SharePoint, Quote Tool, and Executed Contracts folder, and keep budgetary versus firm quoting set up and up to date.

• Analyze platform data to identify trends and generate insights (win rates, where and why we're losing deals by customer, region, or vendor), build vendor scorecards, report on quote tool results, and track KPIs.

• Partner with Sales and Regional Pricing Analysts to shape strategy by region, for example onboarding more vendors, adjusting portfolio in a given country, or using budgetary quoting.

• Work with the Dev team on vendor API onboarding and maintenance, test serviceability and pricing, run monthly proactive testing once new integrations go live, and make sure key vendors' APIs are running correctly.

• Serve as the point of contact for US vendor escalations, platform escalations, and vendor portal access for new joiners, and support MSA revisions and adjustments as needed.

• Lead the project to have vendors submit their own onboarding updates, building lists, and rate cards directly.

• Takes on additional responsibilities and projects as needed to support the success of the team and organization.

What you'll need for success:
Required

• Experience with Sales and/or purchasing/buyer functions; strong Excel skills.

description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with an fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

 

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision https://www.monumental.co/our-vision/and company https://www.monumental.co/about/. You might enjoy Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2-Q2F0Fcx4A, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DOo8n19XEns.

About the role

Over the last few years, Monumental has gone from developing a product that works and delivering our first pilots to building at scale - a fleet of 150+ robots that have laid bricks for 90+ homes, a school, a community centre, a hotel, and 150+ m of canal walls.

We're taking on more construction projects - "deployments" - every month, with more robots, more people, and now in new markets as we scale from the Netherlands into the UK and US.

As Hub Lead, you’ll stand up our first hub outside HQ, in the north of the Netherlands. You’ll start by running our largest deployment to date, then build the team and operations around it as the project pipeline ramps up behind you.

We're hiring versatile operators who want to run a deployment as if it were their own business. Behind every one of these projects is a Deployment Manager who owns it end to end. In practice this is five jobs in one: site foreman, operations manager, account executive, analyst, and project manager. You make the build plan, deploy yourself with your team on site as a subcontractor, manage the contractor relationship, and take responsibility for delivering quality walls, finished on time - in construction, one of the most chaotic industries there is. Your goal will be to run multiple deployments in parallel, overseeing complex and high stakes projects.

One day you're up at dawn, travelling to site, cutting bricks, running the schedule, working with the general contractor and watching your build plan go up brick by brick. The next you'll be at our facility analysing your deployment's P&L and building the systems that improve your margin on the next deployment. You’ll own delivery and translating friction you observe on-site to our R&D team.

This is hard, on-site operations, and some of the most rewarding work you'll find. Robots break, weather turns, the contractor changes the plan, and it's on you to keep the build moving.
You'll have an extraordinary amount of autonomy. It's an excellent fit if you've founded a company before, or if you're looking for an entrepreneurial role where you can make outsized impact.

What you’ll do

- Plan the logistics of a deployment: decide how many and which robots and humans to send, coordinate with other subcontractors, and make both a day-to-day operational plan while also thinking about the bigger picture and how your decisions impact our unit economics.

ABOUT EXPERIENCE BY INDUSTRIOUS

Experience by Industrious is a workplace hospitality brand launched by CBRE - built on the idea that where you work should actually feel like somewhere worth showing up to. We combine CBRE's real estate scale with Industrious' operating model to run dedicated experience teams across office assets, enterprise headquarters, healthcare facilities, and logistics centers worldwide.

ABOUT THE ROLE

A great meeting space is only great if someone makes it feel that way. That's you.

As a Meeting & Event Manager, you're responsible for the full lifecycle of a booking: responding to inquiries, coordinating logistics, running the day-of experience, and making sure the space is ready for the next one. You're the person clients interact with, and the impression you leave is the impression the building leaves.

This role is part sales, part operations, part hospitality. You'll work in Tripleseat, conduct site tours, flip rooms between events, and follow up with clients to make sure they got what they needed. The detail work matters here just as much as the relationship work.

The best people in this role take genuine pride in flawless execution and understand that a smoothly run event isn't just good for the client - it's what fills the calendar next quarter.

WINNING IN THIS ROLE MEANS:

• Every event runs smoothly. Clients leave knowing exactly what they'll tell their colleagues when recommending the space.

• Your Tripleseat pipeline is clean and current - you know what's confirmed, what's pending, and what needs follow-up.

• Clients rebook. They mention you by name. The space gets a reputation as the one that always gets it right.

• Spaces are always reset and ready. No client ever arrives to a room that wasn't prepared for them.

• Revenue is on track. You understand your contribution to the building's booking goals.

YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE AND SUCCEED AT IT IF:

• You take the details personally. A room that's not quite right, a follow-up that didn't happen, a catering order that arrived late - these things bother you because you care about the client's experience, not just your to-do list.

• You're good at managing a lot of moving parts at once. Multiple bookings, multiple vendors, multiple client requests - you have a system, you trust it, and things rarely fall through the cracks.

• You enjoy the client-facing side of this work. Conducting a site tour, answering questions, helping someone figure out the right setup for their event - you're comfortable in those conversations and you do them well.

• You understand that sales and service are connected. The way you handle an inquiry is part of the reason it converts. The way you run an event is part of the reason they rebook.

• You're reliable under pressure. Something goes sideways an hour before an event. You handle it calmly, fix it quickly, and the client never knows it happened.

NOT THE RIGHT FIT IF:

• You'd rather focus purely on one thing at a time. This role requires managing multiple bookings and relationships simultaneously.

• You find the combination of sales activity and event logistics more stressful than energizing.

• Client-facing work feels uncomfortable. A significant part of this role is being the face of the space to people booking it.

• You're not interested in the revenue side of the role. Here, your work connects directly to building performance.

• Repetitive tasks like room resets, daily check-ins, and Tripleseat updates feel beneath you. Here, they're fundamental.

WHAT YOU OWN

General management.

• Submit financial and engagement reporting on time and to standard.

• Monitor trends on a regular cadence so internal teams and asset managers can understand the business.

• Manage amenity budgets.

• Build clear systems and procedures that set the team up for success when you're not there.

• Support marketing teams in keeping collateral and experiences on-brand.

• Support leasing teams in showcasing building amenitie

title: Estate Planning Consultant
description:
Please note: We’re hiring across multiple locations in England, including Edinburgh, London, Yorkshire, Newcastle, Exeter, Cambridge, and more! To apply, you must have a valid UK driving licence, access to a car, and be willing to travel within your local area for appointments.
The Company
We’re Octopus Legacy : one of the fastest growing tech companies in the country, part of the UK’s most exciting and best-trusted group (you may have heard of some of our sister companies…) and we have a mission.
We’re on a path to scale, aiming to become a household name while transforming a long-established industry and helping our customers prepare for, and find support after, death.
But we can’t do it alone, and that’s why we’re assembling a team of top performers to build with us.
Ready to be part of something big?
The Role
We are seeking a dedicated Estate Planning Consultant who will be responsible for conducting home visits to assist clients in the process of drafting and creating wills. You will take the time to discuss your clients requirements in detail, explaining how the use of wills, trusts and lasting powers of attorney can work to protect them, their estate and their loved ones. The ideal candidate will excel in providing personalised and comprehensive guidance to individuals and families, ensuring their wishes are accurately documented whilst showing compassion and care.
Key Responsibilities:

• Conduct in-depth consultations during home visits to understand clients' unique needs, assets, and preferences for estate planning

• Guide clients through the legal aspects of will creation, addressing questions and concerns with clarity and expertise

• Collaborate with legal teams and resources to stay informed about current estate planning laws and regulations

• Maintain a meticulous record-keeping system to track client information, preferences, and any legal documentation

• Support with online Wills and other services within the company when required

• Provide exceptional customer service by offering ongoing support and addressing any post-visit inquiries or adjustments

• Stay abreast of industry trends and best practices in estate planning to enhance service delivery

Who Are You?

• Comfortable being fully remote on appointments (opportunity to be in office outside of appointments)

• Must have a full UK driving license and be willing to drive around London

• STEP qualified (preferred)

• Knowledge of how to write Wills and understanding the legalities

• Knowledge of how LPAs work

• In-depth understanding of Octopus Legacy ’s services and ability to upsell

• Proficient in identifying indicators of concerns related to clients' testamentary capacity

• High levels of empathy, discretion and care

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Active listening skills and the ability to understand the customer’s needs

• Proactive in initiating tasks independently and effectively following instructions

• Flexible schedule to accommodate home visits based on clients' availability

Our Mission
When people think about planning for death they think about wills, life insurance and funerals. We take these cold processes and turn them into something more human. Share more than money: leave voice notes, music, recipes. Shape a legacy that connects you while you're here. And after you're gone.
Founded by Sam after his mum died suddenly, we’re a group of people who work in death because we’ve been affected by it. We know the difference a good plan makes, and what it’s like when there isn’t one.
Death can come between us, leave mess, legal fees, frustration. But it can also make us stronger. We see a world where people talk openly about death, and work out the real meaning of legacy, one that connects to them. We’re here to make that world happen .
Benefits:

• Octopus share incentive scheme.

• Flexible holiday + extra day off for your Birthday.

• Vitality Health & Life Insurance.

• Pension scheme.

• Enhanced parental le

title: Sales Director PJM
description:
Voltus builds power capacity at scale. We provide reliable, clean capacity alongside traditional power plants in wholesale electricity markets. As load growth accelerates, the grid is confronting structural constraints. Speed-to-power and affordability are no longer secondary considerations; they are foundational to economic growth.

Voltus enables faster, cleaner, lower-cost capacity by optimizing existing infrastructure rather than waiting years for new generation to come online. Our sales team builds the customer relationships that make this possible, working directly with the facilities, manufacturers, and institutions whose participation adds capacity to the grid.

The Role

Voltus is seeking a Sales Director for the PJM territory to build and grow a book of commercial and industrial customers across the Mid-Atlantic and Great Lakes region.

Demand response is no longer a niche program. As load growth strains grid infrastructure and wholesale electricity markets evolve, the value of flexible, distributed capacity is increasing. This role puts you at the center of that shift, working directly with the facilities, manufacturers, and institutions whose participation translates into real grid capacity and real revenue for their organizations.

The right candidate does not wait for inbound leads or a warm introduction. They pick up the phone, learn the market, and build their pipeline from scratch. Energy background is not required. The ability to sell consultatively to operational and financial buyers is.

This is a remote role. Candidates must be based in the United States, with a preference for candidates located in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Virginia, Maryland, or New Jersey. Some travel required.

Key Responsibilities

• Prospect and generate your own pipeline through outbound cold calling, email outreach, and self-sourced lead development across the territory

• Own the full sales cycle from initial cold call through contract close on net-new accounts

• Build and manage relationships with Facility Managers, Operations leaders, and financial decision makers at hospitals, universities, large manufacturers, and municipalities

• Educate prospective customers on Voltus ’s demand response programs and translate grid economics into operational and financial value for each account

• Meet activity-based expectations in Q1 and transition into quota-carrying performance from Q2 onward

• Maintain accurate pipeline data, forecasting, and deal activity in CRM

• Collaborate with your Regional Sales Manager and peer SDs to share market intelligence, refine outreach strategy, and improve close rates over time

Desired Qualifications

• Proven track record of self-generated outbound prospecting and closing net-new business. Phone-based cold calling is core to how this team builds pipeline, and candidates whose experience is limited to managing a handed book of business are not a fit for this role.

• Experience selling into commercial and industrial accounts. Existing relationships with hospital groups, universities, large manufacturers, or municipalities in the region are a strong plus.

• Energy industry background is not required. Some of our best performers came from outside the space, but familiarity with energy markets, brokers, or C&I energy buyers accelerates ramp.

• Coachable and feedback-oriented, with a long-term mindset. Year one is a ramp, but the renewal commission structure means your book grows significantly in years two and three.

• Comfortable with self-direction in Q1. Activity metrics drive the first quarter rather than quota.

We work with frontier AI labs and companies across healthcare, finance, and legal providing the specialist knowledge and human oversight that makes AI models more accurate and reliable in these highly regulated domains.

title: National Account Director (Zinc/ Caremark)
description:
Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals , Inc. (Nasdaq ARWR) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company that develops medicines that treat intractable diseases by silencing the genes that cause them. Using a broad portfolio of RNA chemistries and efficient modes of delivery, Arrowhead therapies trigger the RNA interference mechanism to induce rapid, deep, and durable knockdown of target genes. RNA interference, or RNAi, is a mechanism present in living cells that inhibits the expression of a specific gene, thereby affecting the production of a specific protein. Arrowhead’s RNAi-based therapeutics leverage this natural pathway of gene silencing.

Arrowhead is focused on developing innovative drugs for diseases with a genetic basis, typically characterized by the overproduction of one or more proteins that are involved with disease. The depth and versatility of our RNAi technologies enables us to potentially address conditions in virtually any therapeutic area and pursue disease targets that are not otherwise addressable by small molecules and biologics. Arrowhead is leading the field in bringing the promise of RNAi to address diseases outside of the liver, and our clinical pipeline includes disease targets in the liver and lung with a promising pipeline of preclinical candidates.

Arrowhead’s corporate headquarters is in Pasadena, CA with research and development teams in Madison, WI & San Diego, CA, and a state of the art manufacturing facility in Verona, WI. Our employees are nimble, science-driven innovators who are collaborating to bring new therapies to patients in need.

The Position
Let’s do something amazing together! The National Account Director (NAD) will play a critical role in enabling patient access to Arrowhead’s first commercial asset - Redemplo (plozasiran, siRNA targeting APOC3) as well as an expanding pipeline of innovative therapies across multiple therapeutic areas. This product has demonstrated compelling clinical data to date and received approval in November 2025 for the treatment of Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome (FCS). Redemplo (plozasiran) remains in late-stage development for the treatment of Severe Hypertriglyceridemia (SHTG).
The NAD will develop, execute, and manage strategic relationships with key stakeholders across the Zinc (GPO) and CVS Caremark (PBM) books of business, along with their affiliated Commercial and Medicare plan stakeholders, to secure formulary access. The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong individual account management skills and the ability to influence cross-functionally to support Arrowhead’s expanding commercial portfolio. This is a field-based role that requires periodic travel to Arrowhead's Corporate Headquarters in Pasadena, CA, as business needs dictate.

Working through cross-functional teams (CFT), the Senior Category Manager partners closely with plant leadership, R&D, Quality, Operations, Planning, Finance, and senior executives to enhance value delivery through data-driven strategies, strong governance, disciplined negotiation, and creative problem-solving.
The role leads each category through the full TCO sourcing process - from planning and strategy development through sourcing, contracting, supplier qualification, and ongoing performance management - delivering high-impact initiatives that improve operational efficiency, drive structural cost savings, and support Tarkett ’s strategic and sustainability objectives.
Key Responsibilities

• Develop and execute multi-year category strategies for PVC, plasticizers, fillers, recycled PVC, PVB, dispersions, and adhesives that optimize cost, quality, supply assurance, risk, and sustainability performance.

• Lead the full category lifecycle using Strategic Sourcing process - from business case development and market analysis through strategy execution, contracting, and ongoing supplier management.

• Drive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) by applying market intelligence, cost modeling, should-cost analysis, and competitive benchmarking.

• Build and maintain feedstock-to-material cost models (e.g., ethylene/EDC/VCM linkages for PVC; oil and oleochemical linkages for plasticizers) to validate supplier pricing and support fact-based negotiation.

• Negotiate complex supply agreements - pricing, commercial terms, volume commitments, capacity guarantees, and continuity provisions - that secure long-term value and mitigate supply risk.

• Lead Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) for strategic suppliers, including joint business plans, innovation pipelines, and continuous improvement programs.

• Manage the day-to-day relationship and overall performance of managed suppliers, holding them accountable to SLAs, KPIs, and cost targets.

• Develop and manage category KPIs (cost, quality, service, delivery, safety, productivity) and supplier scorecards to ensure measurable value delivery.

• Analyze market and cost-driver dynamics - capacity, feedstock, logistics, trade policy, and regulatory shifts - to anticipate changes in raw material economics and develop mitigation strategies.

• Reduce single-source exposure through dual sourcing, qualified alternates, and regional supply options; maintain category risk assessments and business continuity plans.

• Lead cross-functional stakeholder teams (Operations, R&D, Quality, Finance, Planning, Sustainability) to align sourcing strategies with business goals and secure organizational buy-in.

• Partner with R&D and Quality on material qualification, specification changes, formulation alternatives, and new product introduction (NPI) sourcing support.

• Advance Tarkett ’s circularity and sustainability objectives through recycled PVC and post-industrial/post-consumer content sourcing, supplier carbon and EPD

description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we're changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK's leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We're growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we're hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We're on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own the people engine room at Flock: the employee lifecycle, payroll input, benefits, the HRIS, the office and our in-person events. Your job is to design how a modern People function should work at a company where repetitive admin is automated out of existence and every process is simple, scalable and AI-native by default. You'll report to our Senior People Partner and work with everyone here, from a new joiner on day one to the CEO, who cares deeply about our culture.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

People Operations

- Own the full employee lifecycle: contracts, right-to-work, starter and leaver logistics, probations and changes. Shape the first day and first week alongside managers, delivering a strong employee experience across the lifecycle.

- Be the first point of contact for people queries and audits. Own the People inbox and core HR templates, and drive every query to resolution.

- Own the HRIS (HiBob) and people data: records, workflows, surveys and data integrity. Deliver monthly People reporting and metrics that spot and close gaps early.

- Own payroll input end to end: collate, calculate and submit each month, including bonuses and comp changes. Manage the provider and partner with Finance on reporting and year-end.

- Own benefits end to end as the main contact for providers, systems, data and employee advice, keeping policies and materials current.

- Cut manual effort across the lifecycle by building AI-native workflows, so every routine people process is automated by default, then coach the business to use them. Own continuous improvement across People Ops.

- Partner with IT on joiner and leaver access automation, and on cost and data audits.

Office Management & Socials

- Run the office environment and vendor relationships, including routine upkeep like weekly snack orders and post. Cover health and safety as a trained First Aider and Fire Marshal, and provision hardware fast.

- Own the company social calendar and rituals, from bi-weekly Flock o'Clock (working closely with the CEO) to quarterly Town Halls and larger events, keeping them engaging and on budget.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- Hands-on People or HR Operations experience, ideally in a fast-moving scale-up, with real ownership of end-to-end processes. CIPD or equivalent experience required.

- Hands-on payroll input and benefits administration. HiBob experience is a plus.

- Strong HRIS skills across workflows, automations and integrations, plus confident data and spreadsheet ability.

- Real evidence of building with AI: workflows or tools you've shipped and use, not ones you've only read about.

- Exceptional organisation and judgement. You spot what needs doing and get ahead of it, you build the credibility that lets you influence without leaning on authority, and you treat confidential matters with discretion.

- A quick, first-principles learner who is comfortable with pace, ambiguity and autonomy.

- Working knowledge of UK employment law, compliance and people governance.

- Low ego and high standards. You care most that the work is right and well run.

BENEFITS

- 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Hello, we’re Instrumentl . 👋
Nonprofits do some of the most important work in the world, and most of them are still managing grants in spreadsheets. We're fixing that.
Instrumentl is a profitable, hypergrowth, YC-backed SaaS platform building the operating system for grant-funded organizations. More than 5,500 nonprofits use Instrumentl to discover, track, and win grant funding, from local community organizations to the San Diego Zoo and the University of Alaska. Collectively they’ve moved over $1 billion through our platform.
We're growing quickly, customers love us (check out our G2 reviews!), and we're hiring people who want to build something that matters.
About the role:
We are hiring a Staff Product Designer reporting to the Head of Design. You'll own GrantOS, the foundational layer every other product area at Instrumentl sits on top of: Platform (the data layer, MCP, BI), Core (Tracker, Tasks, Reports, Integrations), and the enterprise surfaces that connect them. This is the seat where you define how grant professionals experience Instrumentl as a system rather than a set of features, which means the data models, permissions, and interaction patterns you set get inherited by every designer and every pod after you. Much of this area is still being invented, so you will be defining problems rather than receiving specs.

What you'll do:

Platform & Systems

• Own end-to-end design for GrantOS across Platform, Core, and enterprise, from discovery through ship and iteration

• Define the data relationships, permission models, and integration surfaces that hold up across every workflow in the product

• Set the interaction patterns and design system foundations that every other product area inherits

• Design how work connects across pods, so a change in one area makes the next one smarter instead of harder
Zero to One

• Drive definition in genuinely greenfield spaces where the right answer is not obvious yet

• Write your own brief, frame the problem, and set roadmap direction in partnership with your PM

• Make good calls with incomplete information and sequence the work so the team ships learnings quickly

• Shape how grant professionals manage tasks, reporting, and integrations across the full grant lifecycle
Research & Influence

• Recruit participants, run the interviews, and synthesize ambiguous user needs into clear product direction

• Bring a point of view into the room and push back when something is not right for users

• Align engineering, product, and GTM on direction at any level of the company

• Raise the quality bar across the design team and coach the designers around you

What we're looking for:

Required

• 10+ years of product design experience with meaningful time at staff or principal level, having owned entire product domains rather than features inside them

• Proven end-to-end ownership of a platform or core product area in complex B2B or enterprise SaaS: data models, permissions, integration surfaces, and patterns that other teams build on top of

• Shipped net-new product work alongside that platform work, including 0-to-1 areas you helped define rather than received as a finished spec

• Deep involvement in user research end to end, from planning and recruiting through synthesis into product decisions

• Experience designing agentic or AI-powered product surfaces
Nice to have

• Design systems experience where you defined the patterns, not only used them

• Prototyping with AI tools, for example building working prototypes in Claude or Cursor that engineers can build from

• Exposure to compliance, data integrity, or workflow-heavy domains

• Startup experience where process was lightweight and you brought your own structure

• Experience mentoring or coaching other designers

• Familiarity with the nonprofit or social impact sector

Compensation & Benefits

For US-based candidates, the target salary range for this role is $200,000 - $230,000 USD , plus equity. Final compensation is determined

As a consecutive interpreter, you will bridge language gaps, ensuring clarity and understanding in various over-the-phone situations.
